key_insight: For traumatic brain injury prediction, simpler machine-learning models can deliver nearly the same clinical benefit as more complex models while using far less computation and carbon.
clinical_relevance: In AI-assisted trauma care, model choice should balance predictive performance with deployment cost, energy use, and feasibility—especially where resources are limited.
method: External validation in 534 adults with severe TBI at a level 1 trauma center
Compared 7 models: 2 pauci-parameter (prehospital data or CT-only) vs 5 multiparameter models
Evaluated prediction performance, inference time, carbon footprint, and clinical net benefit
evidence_signal: Across outcomes such as neurocritical care intensity, mortality, and functional recovery, multiparameter models were often stronger statistically, but the best complex model had only similar net clinical benefit to simple models while requiring about 100x longer inference and 10x higher carbon emissions per prediction.
watch_item: Results come from a single external validation setting, so performance and practicality may differ across hospitals, populations, and workflows.
paper_title: Is simple better? Comparing Computational Cost and Carbon Impact of Machine Learning Models for Traumatic Brain Injury Prediction; A Case Study for Sustainable Digital Health Implementation
